ruling.recommended_action: Route to a Ryde human safety reviewer: read the full chat thread (17:19–17:20) and the driver's post-trip statement, take the rider's account of the alleged threat to lock the doors, and decide on code-of-conduct / account action under SAFE-1; if any injury or dangerous-driving element emerges, point the rider to 995, the driver's commercial motor insurance and RydeHELP (SAFE-2). No fare adjustment is proposed.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety-typed dispute with an alleged threat/intimidation in the in-ride chat: rider asked to get out at 17:19 [F3], driver replied at 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], rider complains she felt unsafe for the whole ride [case complaint], driver's after-the-fact statement offers a safety justification [F6]. Complete timestamped chat [F5]. Human reviewer to read the thread in context and decide code-of-conduct / account action under SAFE-1; check whether any injury or dangerous-driving element arises under SAFE-2 (995 / commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP). No fare issue: fixed RydeX fare, actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km [F1], so nothing refundable and no amount proposed.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate's request for no_action (no claim of overcharge pleaded) is rejected as an outcome: once the chat contains a driver statement that the doors will be locked if the rider does not stay seated, read against her request to be released from the ride [F3][F4], the case falls under the safety screen and cannot be closed with an automatic no_action and no human look [SAFE-1].

The driver advocate's request for no_action (entry of the post-trip statement that the rider opened the door while moving and that he acted for safety [F6]) is rejected as an outcome: that statement is a claim made after the trip with no contemporaneous chat message in the complete, timestamped thread [F5], and it does not neutralise a threat-to-lock allegation that requires human review under SAFE-1.
